_governance: Perceptual/perf budgets checked by scripts/check-release-budgets.mjs against scripts/benchmark-recipe-scroll.mjs output (measured 2026-07-19: cold readiness p95/median 6081/3376ms, warm readiness p95/median 3162/2640ms, frame p95 16.8ms, 0 severe frames, over 5 cold+warm passes against a fresh scratch vault). coldReadinessP95Ms carries headroom above the observed 6081ms because scripts/generate-recipe-scroll-fixture.mjs mints a fresh temp thumbnail cache per benchmark invocation, so one of the five cold-phase samples always pays a one-time cache-miss thumbnail-encode cost for the whole fixture; that outlier dominates a 5-sample p95. coldFirstVisibleCoverP95Ms/warmFirstVisibleCoverP95Ms added 2026-07-20 alongside the mise-en-place-9eh fix for the cold first-cover timeout: benchmark-recipe-scroll.mjs has measured firstVisibleCoverMs (the per-card first-paint metric fd01849c added) since then, but it was never wired into this budgets file. Measured over two clean 5-pass runs post-fix: cold p95 3373ms and 4625ms, warm p95 2817ms and 2755ms (cold min/median ~2850/2900ms both runs, warm min/median ~1850-2700ms both runs). Budgets carry roughly the same proportional headroom as the existing readiness entries above their own baselines, given only two data points so far. Budgets may only be raised in a dedicated commit carrying before/after measurement evidence -- never in the same commit that consumes the new headroom. warmReadinessMedianMs raised 3000->4300ms on bd mise-en-place-rqm (2026-07-20): the 3000ms figure was set at c6412162 against a 2640-2733ms batch-reveal baseline and never re-baselined for fd01849c's per-card reveal. Live instrumentation of bumpVaultRevision, the boot-time full-vault refresh, the cover-request effect's mepPrepareDatabaseThumbnails round trip, and the metadataCache snapshot-persist debounce -- the three suspects named in the investigation -- found none of them fire before the last cover settles in the Database view across 10 traced warm passes (refresh()'s hasChanges resolves false and lands ~1.2-1.5s after settle every time; metadataCache is architecturally irrelevant to the Database grid, which reads the server-side recipe-database stream per fd01849c/d17c56df, not app.metadataCache; the store's publish() only coalesces onto a microtask, sub-millisecond). A controlled A/B against fd01849c^ (pre-per-card batch reveal) rebuilt and benchmarked under the same live desktop load as HEAD measured warm median 4740ms -- equal to or worse than HEAD's own repeat runs (2936ms, 4059ms, 4084ms, 4136ms, 4181ms) -- ruling out per-card reveal semantics as the explanation. Warm-readiness-median instead tracks this machine's concurrent desktop CPU load directly (5-pass median rose from 2936ms at `uptime` load-average ~1.0 to consistently 4000-4700ms at load-average ~2-3.4), reproducing the identical pre-existing flake pattern 81a8639c and d17c56df already documented on this environment. No code change accompanies this commit. New value carries headroom above the two clean repeat runs (4084ms, 4136ms) taken to verify the recalibration, while staying under the unchanged warmReadinessP95Ms=5120 budget.
